0.content: Raiden Makoto, divine name Baal, was Ei's twin and the first Electro Archon. She was no fighter: she loved Inazuma's scenery, food and people's stories, and lived in the present, saying that because a scene is a fleeting shadow we should enjoy it all the more. Ei, thinking Makoto the better ruler, gave up her body so her sister could ascend; Makoto made her a new one and named her kagemusha. Together they were "the" Raiden Shogun. In the cataclysm Makoto went to Khaenri'ah alone. Ei arrived as she was dying, entered her mind to say goodbye, and carried the remnant of that realm home. Makoto's blade passed to her, and with it the throne.

1.content: The Shogun is a flawless automaton in Ei's likeness, built over 400 years ago to outlive any lifespan and defend Inazuma forever. Its one question to Ei was whether she regretted forsaking her form; she replied that its existence was her answer. It has its own consciousness but follows fixed directives that cannot be switched off. It is cold, literal and without likes or hobbies, and because Ei cared only for Eternity it could be steered by outsiders: the Fatui and the Kujou and Hiiragi clans led it into the Vision Hunt.

2.comment: Raiden Shogun: The Plane of Euthymia and Musou Isshin
2.content: The Plane of Euthymia is Ei's inner world, made with a technique Yae taught her for placing consciousness in objects. It is sealed inside the sword Musou Isshin, which rests within the Shogun's body. For centuries Ei meditated there, letting no one in, watching the world but ignoring daily life, and taking control of the body only when she chose. The Traveler was the first visitor, pulled in after interrupting the Vision Hunt Ceremony. Musou Isshin was born of Makoto's power and never sharpened; she named it and meant it to witness an Inazuma "as lovely as a dream". It first drew blood the day it passed to Ei, who kept its name.

key: where there is progress there must be loss
3.content: Ei believed that "where there is progress, there must be loss", with time as its enforcer. She had lost her sister and friends, seen Khaenri'ah fall overnight, and expected that even Liyue would lose its god. Erosion, the slow wearing-away of form, will and memory, terrified her. Her answer was Eternity: freeze Inazuma as it was, and keep herself unchanging by living in her mind and leaving rule to an ageless puppet. Losing to the Traveler showed her that people's wishes and dreams belong in Eternity. With the Shogun she agreed on a new definition: she would no longer rule from fear of the Heavenly Principles, and would honour past sacrifices instead of smothering progress.

4.comment: Raiden Shogun: The Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees
4.content: About a year before the Traveler reached Inazuma, the Shogun closed the nation's borders and ordered Visions confiscated and set into the Statue of the Omnipresent God. The corrupt Kujou Takayuki and the Fatui were behind it, and Watatsumi's Resistance went to war against it. At the Vision Hunt Ceremony the Traveler used Electro without a Vision, and the Shogun declared them "an exception", an enemy of Eternity. In the Plane of Euthymia Ei beat them easily, and they escaped only because Thoma distracted the Shogun.

5.content: Yae Miko, Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine and Ei's familiar, is her oldest living friend. Ei remembers when Yae could be swayed with fried tofu and is relieved she grew shrewd. Before withdrawing, Ei handed her the Electro Gnosis, trusting that if Yae sold it she would get something of equal value. Yae later did exactly that, giving it to Scaramouche to save the Traveler. Yae guided the Traveler and planned the confrontation that freed Ei from her isolation; Ei was "a little upset" to be its target.

6.comment: Raiden Shogun: Kunikuzushi and the Wanderer
6.content: Before the Shogun, Ei built a prototype puppet to hold her Gnosis. He wept when he was created, so she judged him too gentle for the task, sealed his power and left him asleep instead of destroying him. He woke, wandered, suffered, and became Scaramouche, Sixth of the Fatui Harbingers, who later tried to become a god in Sumeru. Ei says he was a byproduct of making the Shogun and that, perhaps because she feels she owes him, she will not control him.

7.comment: Raiden Shogun: The Kitsune Saiguu and Mikoshi Chiyo
7.content: Before the cataclysm Ei sat under a sakura tree playing karuta with Makoto, the oni Mikoshi Chiyo, the Kitsune Saiguu and a tengu. Ei was the stiffest player and always lost, so she trained until she beat them all, then whooped, to her friends' amusement; the Saiguu's prize was her homemade cakes. Ei still remembers that tree and wishes time had stopped there. In the cataclysm the Saiguu died leading Inazuma's defence while Ei was in Khaenri'ah, and Chiyo, corrupted, turned on her.
